Fresh direct neighborhood enumeration all 4-subsets n=5,6,7,8
correctness.rationale: Translate each selected KG(n,2) vertex into a K_n edge, and let H be the selected edge set. A test edge uv has exactly q_H(uv)=|H|-d_H(u)-d_H(v)+1_{uv in H} disjoint selected edges. Thus the ordinary fort rule excludes q=1 on unselected uv and skew fort excludes it on all uv. The submitted structural proof correctly rules out sizes 1,2,3 (consider all simple three-edge shapes), and classifies four-edge H by max degree: degree 4 forces a four-star; degree 3 permits only K_1,3 plus disjoint K_2 when n=6; max degree <=2 implies no mixed positive degrees 1 and 2 and hence C4 or matching4. Cycle and six-vertex claw+edge each have an *inside* selected vertex with exactly one disjoint selected edge and fail skew, while star/matching are skew forts. Independent from graph-neighborhood definitions (not the shape classifier), I enumerated every four-vertex subset for n=5,6,7,8, obtaining ordinary/skew counts (20,5),(135,30),(210,105),(595,385). Shapes give n*C(n-1,4), 3*C(n,4), 105*C(n,8), 60 only n=6. Terminal white fort equivalence establishes both failed-forcing numbers C(n,2)-4; no assertion about all inclusion-minimal forts or higher r.
residual_risks: Unrestricted n proof is combinatorial; finite n<=8 checks alone are not its proof.
Minimum *cardinality* fort and inclusion-minimal fort are distinct notions.

evidence: General Kneser successful skew forcing yields Z^-(KG(n,r)), a minimum successful black seed, not F^- or optimal failure counts.
The 2024 ordinary failed scalar specializes to C(n,2)-4; it does not mathematically force the count or skew structure.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader r-range scalar equalities do not imply even a single optimal extremizer classification; the submitted separate structural case analysis is necessary.

value.rationale: Maximum failed-set multiplicities quantify how many distinct extremal forcing obstructions occur in a classical symmetric graph family; ordinary and skew processes have the same extremal size but provably different optima. The classification explains the n=6 exceptional six-vertex shape and onset of matching configurations n>=8, an intrinsically motivated full all-n census rather than a scalar rebranding.
residual_risks: The known ordinary scalar F is not a novel part; only exact optimizer counts/shapes and skew comparison add value.
